name: HYDRA-UMC-LOCAL-TECHNICIAN
build: Six-phase plan (see the README's own Roadmap section): a local, policy-gated AI technician for the ecosystem itself - observes, explains, diagnoses and proposes maintenance, never acts by generating text. The LLM proposes; a deterministic orchestrator validates against real contracts and a real risk-level policy before anything executes, and the highest-risk levels (privileged change, physical action) are not implemented at all in this delivery. Real build: python -m build (see pyproject.toml).
notes: Scaffolding v0.0.1 - Fase 0 only (inventory and security baseline) of six phases. This delivery defines the tool/risk-level matrix (src/hydra_umc_local_technician/policy/risk_levels.py, six levels INFORM through PHYSICAL_ACTION, the top two genuinely unimplemented), the real JSON Schema contracts every future tool call/proposal must validate against (contracts/*.schema.json: ToolRequest, ToolResult, MaintenanceProposal, EvidenceBundle, PatchVerificationReport - copied field-for-field from those schema files, not invented), a real secret-redaction module ported from HYDRA-UMC-OPS-AGENT's own already-tested log_redaction.py, and this delivery's own literal exit criterion: a real adversarial test proving a malicious retrieved document (a poisoned README/log/doc) can never produce a tool execution or leak a secret, because the orchestrator boundary only ever accepts a real, schema-validated ToolRequest object - free text from an untrusted source is never parsed as a command. No inference engine, no RAG index, no real tool execution, and no HYDRA-UMC-SERVER integration exist yet - those are later phases, see README ROADMAP.
